notes:
- Settings that answer a search: Settings now opens with a search field. Results cover the ten shelves and the parts inside them - Interface's App layout, Card design and Motion, Appearance's Background and Accent colour, and the named cards on Library, Device, Type, Jokes, Seasonal, Account and Updates - so "OLED", "app lock" or "Info page" lands on the page that holds it. Exact and prefix hits rank first, compact spellings like "fullscreen" and "dark mode" still match, a typo falls back to the closest setting, and every matched word is highlighted in the result title and description. An empty search offers five suggestions, and a result opens its page or sub-page directly.
- A second title page, and a switch: Settings > Interface > App layout now offers an Info page choice. Classic keeps the title page exactly as it shipped; Nova draws the redesign. The two choices are independent of the Home and Library layouts, so a reader can keep the new Home and the classic title page, or the other way round - and an install that never touches the switch keeps the classic page. Both pages use the same AniList response, the same entry editor and the same appearance settings.
- The Nova title page leads with the artwork: The key art runs full-bleed from under the status bar, with a round back control, a glass action capsule, the poster and title in a lockup, and the status as a full-width capsule that opens the entry editor. A four-up strip puts score, popularity, favourites and length side by side with the next-episode countdown underneath; the wavy progress bar gets its own card; and a trailer card draws YouTube's own thumbnail instead of hiding the video in a list row. Synopses, details, categories, cast and relations are the same cards the classic page uses, in the reference order.
- One colour from the cover, across the whole page: The Nova hero reads its accent from the artwork actually on screen - BetterPosters when that source is chosen - and uses it for the poster's shadow, the artwork's placeholder and the page's wash, so the first frame is the title's colour rather than a grey slab. The artwork drifts against the scroll in the draw phase, the page backdrop keeps its hand-off at the hero's measured bottom edge, and both title pages keep the docked bar with its read-progress line.
- The entry editor names the title it is editing: The My Entry destination now opens with the title and the draft's status under the heading, and its close control sits on a tonal disc rather than floating as a bare glyph. The form, its pinned Save and Delete bar and its staged edits are unchanged - this is a header retouch, not a new editor.
